gloss: shrine building; main hall of a Shinto shrine

definitions.gloss: shrine building; main hall of a Shinto shrine
definitions.explanation: The main building or buildings of a Shinto shrine where the deity is enshrined. Can refer to the main hall specifically or to the shrine buildings collectively.

examples.japanese: {社殿|しゃでん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{参拝|さんぱい}する→参拝する：15627_sanpaisuru⟧。
examples.english: To worship at the shrine building.

examples.japanese: {朱塗|しゅぬ}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{社殿|しゃでん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{美|うつく}しい→美しい：01121_utsukushii⟧。
examples.english: The vermilion-painted shrine building is beautiful.

examples.japanese: ⟦{火災|かさい}→火災：02561_kasai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{焼失|しょうしつ}→焼失：13480_shoushitsu⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧{社殿|しゃでん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{数年|すうねん}→数年：28206_suunen⟧⟦かけて→かける：00854_kakeru⟧⟦{再建|さいけん}→再建：11743_saiken⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The shrine building that was destroyed by fire was rebuilt over several years.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{社|しゃ}→〜社：04660_sha⟧ (shrine) and {殿|でん} (hall, palace). Refers specifically to Shinto shrine architecture, not Buddhist temples.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Shinto shrine buildings typically include the ⟦{本殿|ほんでん}→本殿：13090_honden⟧ (main hall housing the deity), ⟦{拝殿|はいでん}→拝殿：24252_haiden⟧ (worship hall where visitors pray), and various auxiliary structures. {社殿|しゃでん} can refer to any of these or to the complex as a whole. Traditional shrine architecture features distinctive elements like {千木|ちぎ} (forked finials) and {鰹木|かつおぎ} (log-shaped ridge ornaments).

- {朱塗|しゅぬ}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{社殿|しゃでん} — vermilion-painted shrine building
